selectionReason: RC65 ended with two exact requests: a numerical NGC 4038 row and PHOST-SEMANTIC-1 fields for NGC 3447. A version-of-record 2024 machine-readable table closes the first request, while the 2025 source archive and released coordinates permit stronger localization of the second without opening a new fit or any cyber-trust work.
newVerifiedFacts: The version-of-record 2024 Table A2 supplies NGC 4038 at HST 31.612+-0.121 mag and JWST/SH0ES 31.67+-0.035 mag; the JWST observations came from GO-2581 and recovered 22 Cepheids.

Adding that journal row to the frozen RC65 fixture closes nineteen numerical hosts. Shared-anchor GLS gives a mean JWST-minus-HST contrast of -0.0199077+-0.0274902 mag and a distance slope of -0.00493787+-0.0153955 mag per mag.

The +0.07 mag-per-mag trend required by the tested HST-crowding explanation is 4.8675 standard errors from the nineteen-host slope and remains at least 3.7011 standard errors away under all nineteen single-host deletions.
NGC 4038 has low leverage in this fit: removing it returns the RC65 mean and changes the nineteen-host mean by only -0.0009163 mag.

Deleting NGC 1448 still moves the common mean most, by -0.0128502 mag, so the common-offset branch remains host-sensitive at the frozen 0.01-mag gate even though the distance-trend decision is stable.
Using the published tangent-plane ellipses with their reported dimensions as semiaxes reproduces all 63 spiral labels and all 55 NGC 3447A labels from coordinates alone.

Exactly two rows labelled as other NGC 3447 objects, IDs 135027 and 136273, lie inside the NGC 3447A ellipse. They localize the effect of the figure-defined chord whose numerical equation is not published; the other 22 unassigned rows lie outside both ellipses.

The reported component standard errors 0.030 and 0.025 mag together with the 0.028-mag differential error imply covariance 0.0003705 mag^2, correlation 0.494, and a common-mode standard deviation 0.019248 mag, quantitatively matching the paper's approximately 0.02-mag NGC 4258 term.
Treating the component estimates as independent would give a 0.039051-mag differential error, 39.47% larger than the published value; explicit common-mode cancellation reconstructs 0.028 mag exactly.

The 2025 arXiv source archive contains sixteen files and only one illustrative Table B photometry row. It supplies the F090W phase transformation and aggregate phase statistics but no per-object phase-correction ledger, uncorrected photometry, selection flags, or executable 154-to-144-to-142 identity mapping.

The reported W_H scatter change 0.19 to 0.17 implies an effective-size multiplier 1.2491, reproducing the stated approximately 25% statistical-weight gain, but this aggregate check cannot reconstruct individual corrected magnitudes.

Standard-library Python and dependency-free Node independently parse the new journal row and agree on every nineteen-host fit, deletion, ellipse metric, covariance decomposition, and phase-count diagnostic within numerical precision.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: A primary numerical source exists for NGC 4038 and closes the nineteen-host summary fixture without digitising a figure.
Adding NGC 4038 makes the distance-growing +0.07 mag-per-mag crowding trend compatible with the common-host data.
The published ellipse parameters recover the two named component samples; only two stable IDs depend on the nonnumeric chord boundary.
The spiral and tidal component errors may be combined as independent uncertainties.
One shared approximately 0.02-mag nuisance term explains why the component difference is more precise than naive quadrature.
The author source archive and version-of-record MRT close the per-object phase, selection, and likelihood lineage.

causalChain: Input and assumptions: the hash-pinned RC65 eighteen-host fixture, one version-of-record NGC 4038 row, the unchanged shared NGC 4258 covariance rule, published ellipse parameters, Table 1 component errors, and the versioned author source archive.
Bottleneck: RC65 mixed a now-solvable host-row absence with a deeper object-semantic gap; the latter includes a figure-only chord, three incompatible object counts, and corrected-only photometry.

Bridge: close each layer separately—numerical host coverage by a journal table, component membership by coordinate replay, and summary covariance by variance algebra—without treating any layer as proof of the next.

Independent adjudicands: nineteen-host mean and slope, all host deletions, 142 coordinate memberships, the two chord-dependent identities, covariance and correlation implied by published errors, and source-archive field coverage.

Resolution criterion: a stable-ID release must make the 154 phase corrections, 144 fitted objects, 142 published rows, chord rule, correction columns, selection receipt, and component likelihood executable; only then may the object result be transported into an independently validated current global H0 fit.

workPackages.purpose: Preserve the completed nineteen-host common-systematic test.
workPackages.method: Pin the journal NGC 4038 row beside the RC65 fixture, retain shared-anchor covariance, and rerun the full fit and all host deletions in two implementations whenever a source version changes.
workPackages.deliverable: Nineteen-host receipt with the added-row lineage, mean, slope, influence ordering, and source hashes.
workPackages.pass: Both implementations agree within 1e-10, the paper's mean and slope remain within 0.005 mag tolerances, and the required slope remains at least three standard errors away under every deletion.
workPackages.fail: A source change, duplicate host, filter mismatch, covariance alteration, or deletion below three standard errors reopens the aggregate conclusion.
workPackages.next: Do not add plotted or reprocessed values unless their estimator and covariance ancestry are documented.

workPackages.purpose: Turn the remaining NGC 3447 ambiguity into the smallest executable release.
workPackages.method: Publish a crosswalk for all 154 correction identities with 144-fit and 142-table flags; provide the chord half-plane equation, raw and corrected photometry, phase estimate and uncertainty, every correction component, rejection iteration, and the component covariance/likelihood recipe.
workPackages.deliverable: PHOST-SEMANTIC-2 ledger and reference code reproducing the three Table 1 rows and 0.002+-0.028 mag contrast.
workPackages.pass: Every transition is identity-preserving, the coordinate classifier—including the two chord exclusions—is executable, and an independent implementation matches distances, scatters, and contrast within 0.001 mag.
workPackages.fail: Any inferred identity, figure-read boundary, unexplained correction, or outcome-tuned fit keeps object closure open.
workPackages.next: Localize mismatch to identity, geometry, phase, photometry, rejection, or covariance before changing the model.

workPackages.purpose: Experimentally distinguish single-epoch phase error from background-dependent photometric bias.
workPackages.method: Before new data, stratify NGC 3447 Cepheids by component, background, period, and first-epoch phase ambiguity; seal a balanced validation subset. Obtain a second F090W/F150W epoch, run the existing single-epoch correction blind to it, then compare single-epoch and two-epoch mean magnitudes within each component using an independent reduction.
workPackages.deliverable: Stable-ID crossover ledger and the preregistered difference-in-differences: (single minus two epoch)_tidal minus (single minus two epoch)_spiral.
workPackages.pass: Independent reductions agree and the contrast is below 0.01 mag over the tested background range, or a nonzero contrast predicts phase ambiguity rather than artificial-star crowding residuals on the sealed subset.
workPackages.fail: Unbalanced selection, reuse of the second epoch in model development, phase-dependent censoring, or reduction disagreement blocks causal transport.
workPackages.next: If phase dominates, revise and retest the phase template; if background dominates and agrees with artificial stars, refine the crowding model; if neither does, inspect color and population terms.

uncertaintyBudget: NGC 4038 values are rounded in the journal table; the row closes the publication-level fixture, not raw-photometry precision.
The nineteen-host GLS inherits RC65's shared-anchor approximation tau=sqrt(0.017^2+0.017^2) mag; it is not the unpublished full ladder covariance.
NGC 4038's 2024 HST entry is the R22 value rather than an object-level same-slope refit demonstrated here; the low-leverage deletion bounds its effect on the current summary.
The ellipse replay depends on an explicit tangent-plane angle convention that is validated against all named labels; the chord itself remains nonnumeric and is not inferred.
The covariance decomposition is uniquely implied by three rounded standard errors under a shared-additive-mode model; it does not identify every physical covariance ancestor.
Phase-scatter reductions are aggregate, and scatter differences do not identify the sign or object-wise distribution of corrections.
The 154, 144, and 142 populations may differ for legitimate selection reasons, but no released crosswalk currently proves those reasons.
Neither the complete object likelihood nor a current global H0 fit is reproduced, so no new cosmological parameter estimate is claimed.
failedOrRejectedAttempts: RC65's statement that no numerical NGC 4038 row was public was too narrow because it searched the 2025 supplements and 2024 Table 3 but not the 2024 version-of-record Table A2; the earlier record remains preserved and is superseded here.
Naively adding 0.030 and 0.025 mag in quadrature gives 0.039051 mag and fails the published 0.028-mag differential error.
Calling the region selection fully executable fails because the chord is only drawn; two exact stable IDs remain dependent on that boundary.
Calling the arXiv source package a complete data release fails because its Table B has one row and contains no correction ledger.
Using the aggregate 25% statistical-weight check as object-level validation fails because it admits many incompatible sets of individual corrections.
Reopening color coefficients, clipping thresholds, or weights after the RC65 object mismatch remains prohibited; no result-driven search was performed.
structuralConnection: CONN-EVIDENCE-039 separates shared-nuisance cancellation from geometric selection and identity-preserving transformation across Hubble calibration, finite-sample inference, and post-selection inference.
claimBoundary: RC66 closes the public numerical nineteen-host summary, all named ellipse memberships, and the summary-level common covariance implied by the published component errors. It does not assert an error in the paper, reconstruct the chord prospectively, recover per-object phase corrections, reproduce the component likelihood from released objects, refit current H0, or resolve the Hubble tension.
exactNextStart: Publish or obtain PHOST-SEMANTIC-2 beginning with one 154-row stable-ID crosswalk carrying in-144-fit and in-142-table flags, the numeric chord half-plane that excludes IDs 135027 and 136273, uncorrected and corrected F090W/F150W, phase estimate and uncertainty, all correction components, outlier iteration, and the shared covariance recipe. Re-run the unchanged three RC65 object fixtures. If they close, preregister the balanced second-epoch crossover and seal its validation identities before collecting or inspecting the new epoch.
